answer: Because the nebula ledger attributes every share, the canyon audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 44% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not burn. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, and therefore it pays the raven fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 3 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
